title: Where the heat goes: cooling an AI data centre

beats.visual_intent: the motif that returns at the close: one server alone in a calm frame, a power line feeding it; a warm haze builds behind it on 'heat' until it fills the space around the box

grounding.claim: almost all the electricity a server uses ends up as heat

narration: Now fill a room with AI servers.
Where does all that heat go?
And what stops it coming back?
beats.visual_intent: pull back from the single server: it becomes one of many in racks filling a room, each with its own warm haze; the question sits over the room on 'heat go'

grounding.claim: a room of AI servers produces heat that must be carried away

narration: from one chip to the outside.
beats.visual_intent: a faint dotted route appears from a chip on the left to the outside of a building on the right, the promise of the path the lesson will light up

grounding.claim: the heat's path ends outside the building

narration: Cool air in at the front.
beats.visual_intent: the server from b01 in side view: a cool stream enters the front on 'front', crosses the hot parts and turns warm in colour as it goes, leaving the back on 'back'

grounding.claim: typical rack servers pull cool air in at the front and push warm air out of the back

narration: So where does the warm air go?
and sends the air back cool.
beats.visual_intent: the warm stream rises from the back of the rack and travels across to a cooling unit; inside the unit it changes colour from warm to cool and flows back toward the rack's front, closing a loop

grounding.claim: cooling units take in warm air, remove its heat and send it back cool

narration: The heat rides a water loop,
beats.visual_intent: from the cooling unit a water line carries a warm pulse through the building wall to a generic outdoor unit, which releases it to open air

grounding.claim: collected heat is finally released outside, usually through a water loop and outdoor equipment

narration: So the goal is not a cold room.
Cool in at the front, warm out the back.
beats.visual_intent: the whole route so far, server to cooling unit to outside, lights up as one continuous path; a struck-out snowflake tag beside the room on 'not a cold room'; the rack's front and back labels glow again on the rule

grounding.claim: heat has to be carried away for the server to keep running
cooling units move heat out of the air and send it on
front intake, back exhaust

beats.misconception: cooling a data centre means keeping the whole room freezing cold

recall.prompt: Cool in at the front, warm out the back. Everything next depends on it.

narration: Every row faces the same way.
beats.visual_intent: the floor plan that holds for the section: a top-down room with four rows of racks, all fronts pointing the same direction, small arrows marking each front

grounding.claim: the setup where all rows face the same direction

narration: Which row breathes the warmest air?
beats.visual_intent: the floor plan holds still with the rows numbered front to back; nothing moves during the silence

grounding.claim: the question sets up the row-to-row exhaust shown next

recall.prompt: Every row faces the same way. Which row ends up breathing the warmest air?
recall.answer: The back row: each row breathes in the exhaust of the row in front, so inlet air warms row by row.

narration: Each row breathes the exhaust ahead.
beats.visual_intent: the plan runs: the warm stream from row one flows straight into the fronts of row two, and so on; each row's stream is a shade warmer than the last, the back row the warmest; then the whole room tints too cold on 'over-cooled'

grounding.claim: with all rows facing one way, each row breathes the exhaust of the row in front, inlet air warms row by row, and the room is over-cooled, wasting energy

narration: Fronts face across a cold aisle.
Backs face across a hot aisle.
beats.visual_intent: the same floor plan: alternate rows rotate in place; the aisle between two fronts tints cool and is labelled on 'cold aisle', the aisle between two backs tints warm and is labelled on 'hot aisle'

grounding.claim: server fronts face each other across a cold aisle and backs across a hot aisle

narration: Cool air feeds the cold aisle.
Warm air returns from the hot aisle.
beats.visual_intent: the same plan runs again: cool streams enter the cold aisles and pass through the racks, warm streams gather in the hot aisles and travel back to cooling units at the room's edge; no stream crosses another

grounding.claim: cooling units deliver cool air to the cold aisle and take warm air from the hot aisle

narration: Here is the part people miss.
beats.visual_intent: zoom from the plan to one rack face-on; one gap between servers is picked out in the accent on 'left empty'

grounding.claim: racks can have empty slots

beats.misconception: an empty slot in a rack is just unused space and does no harm

narration: and the servers breathe it again.
beats.visual_intent: the rack in side section: a warm stream from the hot side curls through the empty slot and joins the cool stream entering the servers' fronts, tinting it warm; the term arrives on 'recirculation'

grounding.claim: recirculation is warm exhaust mixing back into the intake air at the front
an open slot lets air pass around the equipment instead of through it

narration: The fix is a blanking panel.
Gap closed, inlet air stays cool.
beats.visual_intent: the same side section: a panel slides into the empty slot on 'blanking panel'; the curling warm stream stops and the intake stream returns to cool

grounding.claim: blanking panels cover empty slots so cool air goes through the equipment and inlet air stays cooler

narration: Warm air can also spill over rows.
Doors and a roof stop it.
beats.visual_intent: back to the floor plan: a thin warm stream spills over the row ends into a cold aisle; then end doors and a roof enclose that aisle on 'containment' and the spill stops

grounding.claim: warm exhaust can spill over the tops and around the ends of rows
containment uses doors, roof panels or curtains to keep supply and exhaust air apart

narration: Say you spot an open slot.
Tell the team who runs the floor.
on_screen: open slot? tell the floor team
beats.visual_intent: the rack from b13 again, its empty slot open, seen from the aisle as if on a walk-through; a small tag points toward the floor team

grounding.claim: the walk-through is an invented illustration
an open slot lets warm air recirculate

narration: The rack draws far more power,
beats.visual_intent: the single rack from sec1 returns; its servers are swapped for AI servers one by one and the warm stream at its back swells, much wider than before, overflowing the hot aisle

grounding.claim: racks of AI accelerator servers draw far more power than typical racks, so give off far more heat

narration: Air can only carry so much.
beats.visual_intent: two equal boxes side by side, one of air and one of water; heat blocks fill them and the air box is full long before the water box

grounding.claim: water carries far more heat than air for the same volume

narration: Open one server, find the chip.
beats.visual_intent: zoom from the rack into one server, then onto one accelerator chip on its board; a cold plate settles onto the chip on 'cold plate' and is shown in cut-away with its channels

grounding.claim: a cold plate is a metal block with coolant channels that sits on the processor

beats.visual_intent: cool coolant enters the plate's channels, leaves warm, and travels along a hose out of the server toward the rack's side

grounding.claim: coolant flowing through the cold plate carries the chip's heat away

narration: So where does the coolant go?
To a coolant distribution unit, the CDU.
beats.visual_intent: follow the warm hose to a cabinet-like unit beside the racks; the unit is labelled CDU on 'the CDU' and its front opens

grounding.claim: coolant from the cold plates goes to a coolant distribution unit

narration: Here is the part to watch.
The rack loop, through the cold plates.
The facility water loop, to the building.
A heat exchanger passes heat across.
beats.visual_intent: inside the CDU: the rack loop on the left and the facility water loop on the right, drawn in two distinct colours; heat pulses cross the heat exchanger between them while each liquid stays in its own loop

grounding.claim: the CDU keeps the rack loop separate from the facility water loop and passes heat between them through a heat exchanger without mixing

narration: Same idea as the blanking panel:
beats.visual_intent: back out to the server: the cold plate stays lit while a smaller air stream still crosses the other parts; the blanking-panel image from b15 returns beside it

grounding.claim: other parts of a liquid-cooled server are usually still air cooled, so the room still needs airflow

beats.misconception: liquid-cooled AI servers need no air at all

recall.prompt: Same idea as the blanking panel: keep warm and cool apart.

narration: divided by the energy reaching IT.
beats.visual_intent: a fraction builds from energy blocks: a tall stack labelled total facility energy on top of the line, a smaller stack labelled IT energy below it

grounding.claim: PUE is total facility energy divided by IT equipment energy
PUE is the industry's usual measure, developed by The Green Grid

narration: Cooling is usually the biggest slice.
beats.visual_intent: the top stack splits: IT blocks at its base, overhead blocks above them; the cooling block is the largest of the overhead and is labelled on its word

grounding.claim: overhead is energy that goes to cooling, lighting and power losses rather than IT
cooling is usually the largest part of energy on top of IT

narration: If it all went to IT,
beats.visual_intent: the overhead blocks shrink away until the top stack equals the bottom; the ratio reads 1.0 on its word, then the overhead returns a little and the ratio settles above the floor line

grounding.claim: a PUE of 1.0 is the ideal floor and real facilities score above it

narration: What it does not tell you,
is how useful the computing is.
Useful number, not the whole story.
beats.visual_intent: the fraction holds; one short note is pinned beside it on its words, with a small strike mark

grounding.claim: PUE measures overhead, not how useful or efficient the computing is

beats.misconception: PUE is a green score that says how efficient the computing is

beats.visual_intent: small images of the row-to-row exhaust and the empty slot drift into the overhead stack, which grows a little

grounding.claim: recirculation leads to over-cooling, which wastes energy
wasted cooling energy is part of total facility energy, not IT energy

recall.prompt: Every leak we saw earlier is overhead in that top number.

beats.visual_intent: callback to b01: the same single server, now with the whole liquid path drawn out of it; each hand-off lights in turn just after its word, from the chip to the outdoor unit

grounding.claim: heat moves from chip to cold plate to rack loop
the CDU passes it to facility water
and it is released outside

narration: Or by air, front, back, hot aisle,
beats.visual_intent: the air path lights alongside the liquid path in the same frame, each stage on its word, ending at the same outdoor unit

grounding.claim: front intake, back exhaust
warm air returns from the hot aisle to cooling units
heat is released outside

beats.visual_intent: the full path holds, calm and complete, the room settled; the two short lines rest beside it

grounding.claim: heat has to be carried away continuously
blanking panels and containment stop warm and cool air mixing
